builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A2Z GameSpec-Bench: How Faithfully Can Coding Agents Generate Games from Game Design Specifications?
summary: Replaces ad-hoc prompting and manual judgment of agent-built applications with a fixed dependency-aware contract (rules, constraints, prerequisite relations) plus code inspection and scenario-replay playtesting for measuring specification faithfulness. Costs include building per-specification contracts, running agent-generated test policies that consume API or GPU budget, and maintaining the evaluation harness across revision rounds. Contract construction can itself be incomplete or mis-specified, agent-generated test policies may miss failure modes or reward test-gaming, and results on game GDDs may not transfer to other application domains.
rationale: The contract-and-replay evaluation pattern is reusable for assessing coding agents on any structured specification, and the targeted-feedback result is directly actionable, but the full benchmark is domain-specific and requires validation on the reader's own workloads before adoption.
technique: Dependency-aware contract benchmark for game-spec coding agents

claims.statement: Replaces ad-hoc prompting and manual judgment of agent-built applications with a fixed dependency-aware contract (rules, constraints, prerequisite relations) plus code inspection and scenario-replay playtesting for measuring specification faithfulness. Costs include building per-specification contracts, running agent-generated test policies that consume API or GPU budget, and maintaining the evaluation harness across revision rounds.
